messages:
Alex: quick heads up — after bringing q4-small-v2 through the quantized onboarding flow, the eval harness runner is nondeterministically flipping which judge wins. Seen in CI and in my laptop runs.
Maria: can you paste the failing logs? is this the judge ensemble step or the tiebreaker logic?
Alex: pasted the core snippet below from the runner log:
```
2026-02-18 09:12:03 runner INFO selected_judges=['lm-judge-1','lm-judge-2']
2026-02-18 09:12:03 judge INFO compute_pairwise -> scores: [0.492, 0.507]
2026-02-18 09:12:03 runner WARNING tie_detected -> invoking tiebreaker
2026-02-18 09:12:03 runner DEBUG tiebreaker RNG seed=None
2026-02-18 09:12:03 tiebreaker INFO final_winner=lm-judge-1
```
I re-ran same eval set 3x; selection changed across runs.
Sam: looks like the tiebreaker is using random.sample / random.choice without a fixed seed. We also changed default for `--deterministic` in runner last quarter, might've left a path unset.
Jin: also worth noting: quantized model outputs have micro-diffs that can flip a narrow win_rate margin. What metric are we relying on? win_rate from judge logits?
Rach: we use a pairwise preference derived from judge probability mass; the runner currently thresholds at 0.5 and defers to tiebreaker for ~0.5±eps. I pushed a quick patch locally to pin the RNG seed in the harness: branch `ml/fix/deterministic-seed` — _locally_ CI is green for a seeded run.
Alex: repro command I used:
```
python runner.py \
  --evalset=onboard/conversational-small.json \
  --judges=lm-judge-1,lm-judge-2 \
  --quantized=true \
  --seed=42
```
With `--seed=42` selection is stable; with no seed it's flipping.
Sam: short-term: pin the seed in the runner by default and document `--seed` in onboarding. Medium-term: add stability gating in CI — run each eval 3 seeds and require top-judge agreement >= 90% across seeds. I'll also add a dashboard panel `eval.judge_stability` and expose `eval.judge_disagreement` Prom metric.
Maria: agree. Also file an infra checklist — ensure Docker image pins deterministic libs (torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic=True, disable cudnn.benchmark, set OMP_NUM_THREADS). Async worker batching/order can still introduce nondeterminism.
Jin: we should also add anchor prompts (golden examples) to the onboarding eval set to detect calibration drift between quantized and fp16 variants. If anchor examples flip, fail the roll-out.
ci-bot: PR 3456 (ml/fix/deterministic-seed) pushed by Rach — CI checks: unit-tests ✅, lint ✅, integration (runner smoke) ⏳
Rach: merging the seed pin after one more infra check. I'll add a small test that runs the tiebreaker path with fixed RNG and asserts identical winner across runs.
Alex: action list:
- Rach: merge seed pin (PR #3456)
- Sam: add CI gating + dashboard panel (est 1d)
- Jin: design anchor prompts & add to onboarding eval (est 2d)
- Maria: infra deterministic checklist + image update (est 2d)
I'll post follow-up in the PR with logs and baseline metrics. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
